items.title: Watch an AI agent get found, fixed, and shipped in 2 minutes with CoreWeave Forge
items.summary: Corey Sanders takes a help desk agent from first agent to best agent, live on the Fully Connected 2026 stage, in CoreWeave Forge. Start building on CoreWeave Forge, free: https://crwv.co/utcVH What you're watching: Corey's IT help desk agent files tickets, sets a priority, and routes them, and sometimes it gets the priority or the routing wrong. Instead of reading conversations one by one, he runs the whole AI loop in one place and fixes it. Chapters 0:00 The agent works, mostly 0:25 CoreWeave Agent Lens finds the pattern: 1.6% of conversations misprioritized 0:46 Asking ARIA what to try 1:01 ARIA recommends serverless reinforcement learning 1:13 Evaluating the new model against the old one 1:56 The new model's lineage 2:10 Run, observe, curate, improve, evaluate, and run again The tools in the demo: CoreWeave Agent Lens records every step the agent takes in production and groups the conversations that fail the same way, so you start with the cases that matter. ARIA, our AI Research & Iteration Agent, reads your runs and traces and answers with a plan, from what went wrong to what to try next. Serverless RL trains the agent against a score with no training cluster to set up and no reward function to hand-write, running in CoreWeave Sandboxes. Evaluations compare the new version with the one you run today, on your own traces, before anything ships. Lineage shows where every model came from, so you can see what changed, why it changed, and whether it actually improved results. CoreWeave Forge is the development layer where teams run the entire AI loop for models and agents, open to any model, framework, or cloud. It launched at Fully Connected 2026 and it's live today: Forge Free to start, and every new account gets a 30-day Pro trial. Why we built it, from Chen Goldberg, EVP of Product and Engineering: https://www.coreweave.com/blog/coreweave-forge-turn-ai-iteration-into-compounding-improvement Your data. Your stack. items.title: Cheaper Tokens Won't Shrink Your AI Bill
items.summary: In episode 1031 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Ish Shah, Director at Dell how cheaper AI tokens won't necessarily reduce your overall AI expenditure. He explains that even with lower individual token costs, the exponential growth in AI usage and complexity means total token consumption keeps growing. This clip highlights the increasing consumption of AI resources despite advancements in efficiency.

items.title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Computer Vision: Wolfram U Course Preview
items.summary: Check out this interactive course on convolutional neural networks for computer vision, taught using Wolfram Language and Notebook technology. Wolfram U instructor Arben Kalziqi gives a taste of what each section covers — from how images are represented internally to neural net encoders, decoders, layers, training and design — along with how Wolfram Language's built-in tools let you take a neural network apart layer by layer and visualize it with a graph-based system, all without leaving your Wolfram Notebook. You'll also see how to pull pretrained and untrained models straight from Wolfram’s Neural Net Repository and adapt them with transfer learning. This course is one of eight in the full Foundations of AI microcredential and includes the Wolfram AI Course Assistant to answer questions as you work through the lessons. Ready to start learning? Enroll at https://wolfr.am/CNNs-for-Computer-Vision. #ConvolutionalNeuralNetworks #ComputerVision #WolframLanguage #MachineLearning #WolframU

items.title: A Guide to Programming in Wolfram Language: Wolfram U Course Preview
items.summary: Take the next step after *An Elementary Introduction to the Wolfram Language* with this course from longtime Wolfram Language developer and Wolfram U Instructor David Withoff. Half the course dives into the language's inner workings—expressions and evaluation, patterns, transformation rules, attributes and local variables—with a focus on speed and memory efficiency. The other half covers higher-level functions for graphics, numerical computation, algebra, image processing, geometry and time series. Enroll at https://wolfr.am/Guide-to-Programming-with-WL for the full course, plus the Wolfram AI course assistant to help along the way. #WolframLanguage #Programming #WolframU #Mathematica #codingtutorial

items.title: How Many Iterations Does a Good Spec Need?
items.summary: A strong specification rarely emerges fully formed. It improves through focused iteration—clarifying assumptions, resolving ambiguity, testing edge cases, and aligning the intended outcome with real constraints. Hari Krishnan, author of Spec-Driven Development, explains how teams can refine a specification and why there’s no universal number of iterations. The goal isn’t perfection—it’s reaching the point where developers and AI coding agents have enough shared context to implement the right solution confidently. Learn more about Spec-Driven Development: https://hubs.la/Q04ypXVz0 #SpecDrivenDevelopment #AICoding #ContextEngineering #SoftwareDevelopment #CodingAgents #Shorts

items.title: SLMs, Fine-Tuning & LLMOps: Building Production-Ready Language Models
items.summary: Not every use case needs a large model. Smaller and purpose-built is often faster, cheaper and better suited to the job. Terms covered: - SLM (Small Language Model): fewer parameters, trading breadth for precision. Runs on-premises or on edge devices with no cloud dependency. - SLM Development: designing, training and optimizing a small model for a well-defined task or dataset - Fine-Tuning Engine: taking a pre-trained model and training it further on domain-specific data, so it learns the language of law, medicine or your business - LLMOps: the infrastructure and practices for deploying, managing, monitoring and updating language models over time A hospital running clinical documentation on local servers. A manufacturer processing quality reports on factory floor devices. These are where compact models win. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #SLM #FineTuning #LLMOps #AIGlossary #H2Oai

Not every use case needs a large model. Smaller and purpose-built is often faster, cheaper and better suited to the job.

Terms covered:
- SLM (Small Language Model): fewer parameters, trading breadth for precision. Runs on-premises or on edge devices with no cloud dependency.
- SLM Development: designing, training and optimizing a small model for a well-defined task or dataset
- Fine-Tuning Engine: taking a pre-trained model and training it further on domain-specific data, so it learns the language of law, medicine or your business
- LLMOps: the infrastructure and practices for deploying, managing, monitoring and updating language models over time

A hospital running clinical documentation on local servers. A manufacturer processing quality reports on factory floor devices. These are where compact models win.

—
